deeptip.about.title: DeepTip
deeptip.about.short: Explanations with depth: highlighted terms open further explanations.
deeptip.about.body:
A DeepTip explains a control. Highlighted [[deeptip.term|terms]] inside it open another window when you hover them, and a click [[deeptip.pin|pins]] it. Read as deep as you like.

Controls: [[deeptip.mouse|mouse]], [[deeptip.touch|touch]], [[deeptip.keyboard|keyboard]], [[deeptip.gamepad|gamepad]].

deeptip.term.title: Highlighted term
deeptip.term.short: Has its own entry – hover to see it.
deeptip.term.body:
A highlighted term has its own entry. Hover it and a preview appears next to the window; move away and it disappears again. A click [[deeptip.pin|pins]] the window.

If the same term is already open further up the chain, that window flashes instead of opening a second one.

deeptip.pin.title: Pin
deeptip.pin.short: A pinned window stays open until you close it.
deeptip.pin.body:
A pinned window stays open until you close it – with the X, with `Esc` or with **B** on a gamepad. It has a coloured border and a filled pin.

To pin: click a [[deeptip.term|term]], click inside a preview, or press the pin.

Close all windows: hold `Esc` or press `Shift+Esc`.

deeptip.mouse.title: Mouse controls
deeptip.mouse.short: Rest to open, click to pin.
deeptip.mouse.body:
- Rest the pointer on a control: the first window opens after a moment.
- Hover a [[deeptip.term|term]]: its preview appears at once.
- Click a term: [[deeptip.pin|pin]] it.
- On the way into a window the pointer may briefly leave it – as long as it moves towards the window, the window stays.

deeptip.touch.title: Touch controls
deeptip.touch.short: Long-press to open, tap a term to follow it.
deeptip.touch.body:
- Long-press a control (about half a second, the device vibrates briefly): its window opens [[deeptip.pin|pinned]].
- Tap a [[deeptip.term|term]]: its window opens.
- Tap outside or swipe a title bar down: all windows close.

deeptip.keyboard.title: Keyboard controls
deeptip.keyboard.body:
- `F1` or `?` on the focused element: open its window.
- `Tab` moves to the [[deeptip.term|terms]], `Enter` opens one.
- `Esc` closes the current window; hold it or press `Shift+Esc` to close all.
- `F6` switches between open windows.

deeptip.gamepad.title: Gamepad controls
deeptip.gamepad.short: Y opens, A follows, B closes.
deeptip.gamepad.body:
- **Y / △** on the selected element: open its window.
- **D-pad / left stick**: move from [[deeptip.term|term]] to term.
- **A / ✕**: open a term.
- **B / ○**: close a window, hold to close all.
- **LB / RB**: switch between windows.

hw.gpu.title: Graphics card (GPU)
hw.gpu.short: Renders graphics and runs AI models – its memory matters most.
hw.gpu.body: The graphics card runs thousands of small tasks at once, which makes it far faster than the processor for image, video and language AI. How large a [[ai.model|model]] it can handle depends mostly on its [[hw.vram|video memory]].

hw.vram.title: Video memory (VRAM)
hw.vram.short: Memory on the graphics card – decides which models run fast.
hw.vram.body:
VRAM is the [[hw.gpu|graphics card's]] own memory. An [[ai.model|AI model]] only runs fast if it fits completely. When it is full, parts move to [[hw.ram|system memory]] ([[ai.offload|offloading]]) – that works, but is often many times slower.

With 8 GB, smaller or [[ai.quantization|quantized]] models help.

hw.ram.title: System memory (RAM)
hw.ram.body: Running programs live here – and the parts of [[ai.model|models]] that do not fit into [[hw.vram|video memory]]. When RAM runs out too, Windows falls back to the [[sys.pagefile|page file]].

sys.pagefile.title: Page file
sys.pagefile.short: Disk space Windows uses as spare RAM.
sys.pagefile.body: An area on the SSD that Windows uses to extend [[hw.ram|system memory]]. Much slower than RAM. RAM plus page file is the limit for [[sys.commit|committed memory]].

sys.commit.title: Committed memory (commit)
sys.commit.short: How much memory Windows has promised to programs.
sys.commit.body:
Windows promises memory to every program before it is actually used. The limit is [[hw.ram|RAM]] plus [[sys.pagefile|page file]]. When it is reached, programs can crash even though Task Manager still shows free RAM.

Long uptime and [[sys.wsl|WSL]] push it up; a restart resets it.

sys.wsl.title: WSL
sys.wsl.short: Windows Subsystem for Linux – a Linux running inside Windows.
sys.wsl.body: Some AI tools and Docker run in WSL. WSL likes to keep [[hw.ram|memory]] as cache even when it no longer needs it – dropping the cache or shutting WSL down gives it back.

ai.model.title: AI model
ai.model.short: A file of learned weights, e.g. an image or language model.
ai.model.body:
A model is the “brain” of an AI: a large file of learned weights. Its size and [[ai.quantization|quantization]] decide how much [[hw.vram|VRAM]] it needs.

Kinds: [[ai.checkpoint|checkpoint]] (images), [[ai.lora|LoRA]] (add-on), [[ai.llm|language model]] (text).

ai.checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
ai.checkpoint.body: A complete image model such as Flux, Qwen-Image or SDXL. It sets the basic style and quality; [[ai.lora|LoRAs]] adapt it. Usually runs in [[ai.comfyui|ComfyUI]].

ai.lora.title: LoRA
ai.lora.short: A small add-on that tunes a model to a style, character or object.
ai.lora.body: A LoRA adapts a [[ai.checkpoint|checkpoint]] – to a drawing style, a character or a product – without replacing the model. It is small (a few MB to a few hundred MB) and can be trained on your own images.

ai.llm.title: Language model (LLM)
ai.llm.short: An AI model for text: chat, translation, better prompts.
ai.llm.body: A [[ai.model|model]] for language. It answers questions, summarises, translates or expands [[ai.prompt|prompts]]. Locally, language models run for example through [[ai.ollama|Ollama]].

ai.prompt.title: Prompt
ai.prompt.short: The text description a model generates from.
ai.prompt.body: Describes what should be created. Image models usually understand English best; a [[ai.llm|language model]] can expand a short idea into a detailed prompt.

ai.comfyui.title: ComfyUI
ai.comfyui.short: Runs image, video, 3D and audio models as a node graph.
ai.comfyui.body: ComfyUI runs locally and executes [[ai.workflow|workflows]]: nodes load [[ai.model|models]], process the [[ai.prompt|prompt]] and save the result. Other programs send it workflows through its API.

ai.workflow.title: Workflow
ai.workflow.short: A saved node graph in ComfyUI.
ai.workflow.body: A chain of nodes in [[ai.comfyui|ComfyUI]] – load model, prompt, sampler, save – stored as a JSON file and reusable any number of times.

ai.ollama.title: Ollama
ai.ollama.short: A local server for language models.
ai.ollama.body: Ollama loads [[ai.llm|language models]] into [[hw.vram|video memory]] on demand and frees them after a while without use. Programs talk to it through a local API.

ai.quantization.title: Quantization
ai.quantization.short: Model weights with fewer bits – smaller, slightly less precise.
ai.quantization.body: A [[ai.model|model's]] weights are stored with 8 or 4 instead of 16 bits. The model becomes much smaller and fits into less [[hw.vram|VRAM]], but loses some quality. Common formats: `GGUF`, `FP8`, `NF4`.

ai.offload.title: Offloading
ai.offload.short: Model parts in RAM instead of VRAM – works, but slower.
ai.offload.body: When a [[ai.model|model]] does not fit into [[hw.vram|video memory]], parts stay in [[hw.ram|system memory]] and are moved over when needed. Large models run on small cards this way – only slower.

ai.mcp.title: MCP
ai.mcp.short: A standard that lets AI assistants use a program's tools.
ai.mcp.body: The Model Context Protocol connects assistants like Claude to programs. A program announces its tools – such as “generate image” or “free VRAM” – and the assistant can call them.
